inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,924 logical lines. The source develops a chain from the crossing-symmetrized Veneziano amplitude's zeta-ratio representation to a phase-based Volchkov criterion, then derives its relation to Li coefficients, a Chebyshev-kernel hierarchy, and a Fourier-transform form. It also supplies useful negative evidence: non-trivial zeros cancel from the bare zeta ratio, the symmetric modulus limit loses critical-line information, and principal-phase jump terms cancel the desired signal in the symmetric phase limit. Formula extraction is imperfect but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjacent displayed equations; exact formulas should remain tied to the normalized span.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata, abstract, and navigation; the abstract announces the amplitude, integral-criterion, Li, and generalization program.

sections_inspected.label: 1 String Theory and the Riemann Zeta Function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates the physical bridge, derives the crossing-symmetrized amplitude as a zeta ratio, and isolates both the cancellation of non-trivial zeros and the phase-based route that remains.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Statements Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States logarithmic and argument integral criteria, compares two kinematic limits, and constructs the dressed amplitude whose phase yields the Volchkov–Veneziano equivalence.

sections_inspected.label: 3 The Volchkov Criterion Revisited
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the xi Hadamard product, zero-counting Stieltjes sum, convexity equality condition, and explicit Volchkov integral.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1 Relation to Li's Criterion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies Volchkov as the first Li-coefficient integral and connects zero sums to Li positivity.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Generalizing the Volchkov Criterion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs Chebyshev kernels for all Li coefficients, argues the if-and-only-if equality mechanism, controls boundary terms, evaluates average terms, and states integral/positivity corollaries.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3 An Integral Transform
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Rewrites the rational Volchkov kernel through a Fourier transform to express the criterion as a moment of the amplitude phase transform.

sections_inspected.label: 4 A Physical Picture
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates spectral and phase information, recasts the criterion as nested path-integral operations, and proposes explicitly conjectural nonlocal and holographic interpretations.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A Veneziano and Balazard–Saias–Yor
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows modulus symmetry cancels the zeta signal in the symmetric limit and evaluates the residual gamma integral independently of RH.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B A Subtle Phase
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tracks principal-argument branch jumps, regularized gamma contributions, zero-counting corrections, and numerical certification of the cancellation obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix C The Virasoro–Shapiro Amplitude
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers the open-string amplitude phase criterion to the closed-string amplitude through the open/closed amplitude relation.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix D Representations of the Li Coefficients
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives generating-function, zero-sum, and derivative representations of Li coefficients.

accepted_units.title: From spectral realization to an amplitude-phase criterion

accepted_units.context_note: Keep the contrast between spectral realization and integral/phase realization; the authors do not claim to construct the Hilbert–Pólya operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; the extracted half-shifted operator notation at lines 78–80 is formula-risky but the strategic contrast is clear.

accepted_units.title: Crossing-symmetrized four-point Veneziano setup
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the Beta-function amplitude, Regge variables, crossing symmetrization, and the linear constraint required by the later zeta rewriting.
accepted_units.context_note: This is local setup for Proposition 1; retain the s,t,u constraint with the definition of the symmetrized amplitude.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed Beta/Gamma formulas and trajectory constants are text-layer formula dependent; prose establishes their roles.

accepted_units.title: Crossing symmetry converts Gamma structure into zeta ratios
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the Freund–Witten form and explains the reusable mechanism: a triple channel sum creates Gamma ratios to which the zeta functional equation applies, while an unsymmetrized amplitude cannot make the conversion.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact identity depends on the trajectory sum constraint and full crossing symmetrization; lines 263–270 are the conceptual compression of the calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy Gamma/reflection/duplication derivation with imperfect fraction extraction; preserve the exact span for equation-level use.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard pairing removes non-trivial zeros from the bare amplitude ratio
accepted_units.why_material: Uses functional-equation pairing of zeros to explain why the non-trivial-zero product telescopes out, sharply limiting what the bare amplitude spectrum can encode and motivating a phase-based route.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed dual unitary reinterpretation at lines 304–313 is explicitly conjectural, not evidence that such a system exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Hadamard quotient formula is extraction-risky, but the pairing, cancellation, and limitation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: RH integral criteria and two amplitude limits
accepted_units.why_material: Places the Balazard–Saias–Yor and Volchkov criteria beside the zeta-ratio amplitude and identifies two kinematic limits whose information content can be tested.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. Its conclusion requires the immediately following dressed-amplitude construction, recorded as a context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several integral kernels and zeta/Gamma ratios are formula dependent; prose reliably distinguishes modulus and argument criteria and limits A/B.

accepted_units.title: Dressed Veneziano phase as an RH-equivalent criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Removes a zero-free boundary ratio from the asymmetric amplitude so its argument is exactly twice the critical-line zeta argument, yielding the Volchkov–Veneziano if-and-only-if integral.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. Read with lines 393–399 for the asymmetric amplitude being dressed and retain the no-branch-correction qualification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition and weighted integral are displayed-formula dependent; checked prose supports the zero-free dressing and phase identity.

accepted_units.title: Xi-function Hadamard product and functional symmetry setup
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs the entire xi function, its canonical product and logarithmic derivative, then applies functional symmetry to set up a zero-sum invariant.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. The invariant and RH equality mechanism only close in lines 520–578, recorded as a context repair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Canonical-product and log-derivative equations are formula-layer dependent, with coherent surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: Zero-sum invariant and convexity force critical-line equality
accepted_units.why_material: Turns functional symmetry into the constant zero sum −B and compares it with a Stieltjes-weighted zero-counting sum; strict equality in the paired convexity bound occurs exactly on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: Continues the carried Hadamard setup and supplies its missing semantic payoff; the source's phrase 'unconditionally upon RH' is internally awkward, but the next sentences clearly distinguish the unconditional B identity from RH-dependent equality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive zero sums and rational kernel; the convexity/equality logic is recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Decomposing zero count yields the Volchkov integral
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the smooth Gamma and average contributions in the zero-counting identity so the remaining oscillatory critical-line phase integral equals the fixed constant exactly when the zero-sum equality holds.
accepted_units.context_note: Read after the convexity criterion; the term-by-term evaluations are part of the normalization, not a new independent RH argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral constants are displayed-formula dependent and should be checked against the normalized source when instantiated.

accepted_units.title: Volchkov is the first Li-coefficient integral
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the zero-counting integration kernel to Li's coefficients and identifies the Volchkov sum and integral as the n=1 case of the Li hierarchy.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the Li positivity criterion and the Chebyshev integral representation needed for the n=1 identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient definitions and kernels are formula dependent; the n=1 correspondence is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Chebyshev kernels extend the Volchkov construction
accepted_units.why_material: Designs a family Gn whose derivatives match Li's Chebyshev kernels, with a convergence constant that also makes positivity visible.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit proposes the generalized representation; its converse and boundary control are established in the following unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact first/second-kind Chebyshev formulas are extraction-sensitive but their roles and n=1 reduction are clear.

accepted_units.title: Why the generalized zero-height sum is equivalent to RH
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts an unconditional Li zero sum that sees full zeros with a height-only Chebyshev sum, argues equality forces real part one-half, and verifies the Stieltjes integration boundary term vanishes.
accepted_units.context_note: The converse is presented through a formula-dense comparison; preserve the authors' claimed if-and-only-if status rather than strengthening it independently.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk in equations (3.22)–(3.27); prose supplies the information-loss contrast, prefactor obstruction, equality condition, and asymptotic boundary argument.

accepted_units.title: Average zero-count contribution from the Chebyshev generating function
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the generalized integral into average and oscillatory pieces and uses the Chebyshev generating function to evaluate the first average contribution uniformly in n.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a reusable parameter-family evaluation mechanism, not merely a single numerical integral.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy generating-function calculation; exact coefficients require scan/text verification.

accepted_units.title: Digamma expansion evaluates the second average contribution
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the endpoint term, converts the Gamma contribution through a digamma series, and extracts a closed coefficient formula using a generating function and Pochhammer simplification.
accepted_units.context_note: The long coefficient extraction supports the constants in the generalized Li integral; it should not be treated as conceptual evidence independent of the displayed formulas.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very formula-dependent text layer with nested sums; retain the full span and verify equation transcription before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Li integral equality and positivity corollaries for every n
accepted_units.why_material: Packages the preceding construction into RH-equivalent equality and positivity statements for all Li coefficients, explicitly recovering Volchkov at n=1.
accepted_units.context_note: Constants and kernel definitions live in the preceding accepted units; this span is the compact result statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed integral and Chebyshev kernel are formula dependent but well anchored by prose.

accepted_units.title: Fourier representation of the amplitude-phase criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why the rational kernel is unusually tractable and rewrites it via a Fourier transform, turning the criterion into a weighted moment of the transformed amplitude phase.
accepted_units.context_note: Oddness of both kernel transform and dressed-amplitude phase justifies extending the integral to the real axis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier conventions, signs, and constants are formula sensitive; the representation-change mechanism is clear.

accepted_units.title: Spectrum sees trivial zeros while phase carries the criterion
accepted_units.why_material: States the central representational distinction: the usual string spectrum reflects trivial zeros, whereas the scattering phase supports the RH-equivalent sum rule.
accepted_units.context_note: The analogy to Friedel-type phase-shift sum rules is motivational and does not establish a physical realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant with low representation dependence.

accepted_units.title: Integrating momenta first suggests a nonlocal effective worldsheet theory
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts the criterion as worldsheet integration followed by phase extraction and momentum integration, then reverses the integration order to motivate an effective nonlocal action and a possible holographic phase computation.
accepted_units.context_note: The reversed-order 'Riemann string' is a formal proposal; the authors flag phase extraction from the generating functional as the delicate unresolved step.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Path-integral displays are extraction-sensitive; prose clearly specifies the sequence and proposed reordering.

accepted_units.title: Candidate Riemann-string amplitude and dual Regge questions
accepted_units.why_material: Proposes replacing Gamma/Beta amplitude structure by a xi analogue and identifies concrete speculative routes—holography, p-adic rewriting, and evaluation at non-trivial zeros—while marking them as conjectural.
accepted_units.context_note: Do not promote these research questions to established mechanisms or evidence for RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The candidate Beta-to-xi quotient analogy is formula dependent; surrounding limitations are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Physical reformulation is not an RH solution
accepted_units.why_material: Explicitly bounds the paper's claim to a potentially useful physical reframing and denies that it solves RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Important negative constraint for any downstream synthesis of the paper's more speculative passages.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only.

accepted_units.title: The symmetric modulus limit cancels the critical-line zeta information
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates that conjugation makes the critical-line modulus terms cancel in limit A; the surviving exact Gamma integral is RH-independent, so an elegant closed form is diagnostically uninformative.
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix is negative evidence about representation choice, not an alternative RH criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy integral and infinite-product evaluation; the cancellation and RH-independence are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Principal phase introduces zero-dependent jump corrections
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the symmetric-limit amplitude phase and makes the integer branch correction explicit, noting that it jumps at critical zeros and is essential for convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: The correction cannot be dropped by naive additivity of arguments; its later identification drives the cancellation obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Argument identities and Gamma ratios are formula dependent; branch conventions are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Regularized Gamma-phase integral cancels a divergent series
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces an epsilon regulator for the digamma pole, integrates the phase identity, and isolates a divergent sum whose exact cancellation makes the limiting expression finite.
accepted_units.context_note: This is supporting machinery for identifying the branch correction, with a later numerical check; preserve epsilon-to-zero ordering.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense formula extraction with nested integrals and sums; exact constants need source-span verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero-counting branch term erases the Volchkov signal in symmetric limit A
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the branch integer as 1−N(T) and shows its zeta-argument component exactly cancels the explicit zeta phase, explaining why case A cannot encode RH through Volchkov.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the decisive contrast with asymmetric dressed case B and should accompany any use of the two kinematic limits.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Zero-counting formulas are displayed-equation dependent; the exact cancellation conclusion is clear.

accepted_units.title: Numerically checking a branch-sensitive Gamma integral
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how to replace a numerically unstable principal-argument evaluation by LogGamma and an absolute-value identity, then compares analytic and numerical values to thirteen decimal places.
accepted_units.context_note: This validates the appendix manipulation only; it is not evidence for RH or for the physical conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Software-specific and formula dependent; the stability-motivated representation change is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Virasoro–Shapiro phase inherits the Volchkov criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the closed-string amplitude using zeta functional identities, relates it to the squared open-string amplitude with tangent factors, and derives a phase relation allowing substitution into the dressed criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The transfer depends on rescaled Regge variables and the specific asymmetric limit; preserve those qualifications.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula dependence and some broken hat notation in extraction; conceptual open/closed transfer is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard product yields Li generating, zero-sum, and derivative forms
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the Li coefficients both from a transformed xi generating function and from derivatives at one, tying the paper's integral hierarchy back to equivalent canonical definitions.
accepted_units.context_note: The authors state these careful-factor formulas supersede their earlier integral representation; this local source supports only the displayed equivalence derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy product differentiation; exact indices and factorial factors need text/scan checking.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Crossing symmetry plus phase extraction yields the physical criterion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Full channel symmetrization first exposes a zeta-ratio amplitude, but the RH-sensitive statement appears only after choosing the asymmetric limit, removing a zero-free factor, and retaining the phase.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a reformulation conditional on established analytic identities, not a string-theoretic proof or a Hilbert–Pólya construction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Volchkov sits inside a Chebyshev–Li hierarchy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A zero-counting Stieltjes transform, the xi Hadamard invariant, and Chebyshev kernels organize the n=1 Volchkov equality as the first member of an all-n Li-coefficient family.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact all-n converse is formula-dense in this extraction and should be checked equation by equation before formal reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Representation choice determines whether zero information survives
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The bare zeta ratio, symmetric modulus, and symmetric principal phase each erase non-trivial-zero information by different symmetries or branch corrections, whereas the dressed asymmetric phase preserves the Volchkov signal.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is specific to the representations and limits analyzed; it does not rule out other modulus or phase constructions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Integral transforms connect amplitude phase to prospective effective actions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Fourier form and a formal reordering of momentum/worldsheet integration suggest how an RH-equivalent phase sum rule might be represented by a nonlocal or holographic effective action.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The effective Riemann string and its computable phase functional are explicitly unresolved conjectures, and the paper disclaims an RH solution.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Open/closed amplitude relations transfer the phase criterion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Kawai–Lewellen–Tye-type relation supplies an explicit phase identity through which the open-string Volchkov criterion can be restated with the closed-string Virasoro–Shapiro amplitude.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer uses specific Regge rescaling and kinematic limits and should not be generalized to arbitrary amplitudes without new evidence.
